summary: Iteration 2 focused on the new admin editors (pricing, website content, portfolio manager with direct media upload) and public-site integration. Added /app/backend/tests/test_admin_editors.py (11 tests) covering: auth guards for /api/admin/site-settings, /api/admin/media POST, and /api/admin/projects (all return 401 unauthenticated); GET/PUT site-settings round-trip; pricing update reflected in /api/site pricing AND /api/calculator estimates (base + per_page + rush_multiplier math verified for social service); website editor hero description update reflected publicly; social media marketing service present in seeded services; media upload PNG round-trip through /api/media/{id} proxy (valid 1x1 PNG constructed in-test, image/* content-type preserved); text/plain rejected with 415; portfolio project creation with uploaded cover_image visible on public /api/site with same media URL. Full pytest suite (backend_test.py + test_admin_editors.py) now 30/30 passing. UI regression on external preview URL: admin login, admin dashboard renders all editors (pricing, website, portfolio, publishing), pricing editor shows current values (social=30000, per_page=4500, rush=1.25), changing social price to 37777 + save + restore worked (verified via API — /api/site pricing reflected the change during test and was restored to 30000 after), portfolio image upload UI shows 'Media attached' status and Publish project succeeded, published project visible on public / and its image URL is /api/media/{id} (image element present). Mobile 390px layout has 0px horizontal overflow with the new pricing section; social media marketing card + founders (Smaranjit, Diganta) + contact email + phone (+91 97740) all render on mobile.

minor.issue: SiteSettingsUpdateRequest.settings is typed as an unconstrained dict — an admin could send arbitrary/partial settings and wipe out required nested keys (e.g. remove calculator or services), which would then 500 on /api/site and /api/calculator via KeyError. Consider a stricter Pydantic model or a merge/validate step.

Downloads bytes and returns them fully in-memory (no streaming, no Cache-Control/ETag). Fine for 25MB images, but every project image render on the public homepage re-fetches from Emergent object storage — heavy hit as portfolio grows. Add caching headers or CDN in front.

storage.py init_storage() caches storage_key in a module-level variable but is NOT threadsafe; on cold start under concurrent uploads two threads may both POST /init. Low probability but worth a lock.

ui_bugs.issue: React duplicate key warning 'Encountered two children with the same key, TEST Portfolio' — projects are mapped with key={project.title}; multiple projects sharing the same title (which is possible via admin) collide. Use project.id/_id or project.slug fallback.

submit() rebuilds the entire pricing list from calculator base_prices (labels map). Any pricing entry that was originally curated (e.g. custom name/note) will be overwritten with the label-map name and 'Custom scope available' note unless a match by exact name existed. Non-destructive merge would be safer.
Services textarea parser is `|`-delimited and hard-coded to 2 fields; a stray `|` inside a description silently drops the row. Consider a repeater UI or escape.

Uses hard-coded process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL prefix when composing the cover_image (e.g. `${BACKEND_URL}/api/media/{id}`) — persists an absolute URL that will break if the app is later served from a different origin. Storing just the relative `/api/media/{id}` and letting the frontend resolve at render time is more portable.
No image preview after media upload — status text only reads 'Media attached'. A small thumbnail would confirm the correct file was selected before publishing.

issues: Editors are stacked in a wide grid that requires scrolling; a sticky in-page nav or accordion (Overview / Portfolio / Publishing / Pricing / Website) would help non-technical admins find the right editor quickly.

No horizontal overflow with the new pricing section (verified 0px). Contact and founders still render correctly. Mobile nav drawer background transparency called out in iteration 1 was not re-checked here — still an outstanding item.

action_items: HomePage.jsx: use a stable unique key for project mapping (project.id/_id, slug, or index) to remove the React duplicate-key warning triggered by projects sharing titles.
PricingEditor.jsx: do a non-destructive merge on save so custom pricing name/note fields curated in the DB are preserved.

Validate PUT /api/admin/site-settings with a strict Pydantic model to prevent an admin (or bad client) from wiping required nested keys (calculator, services) and breaking /api/site and /api/calculator.
Add Cache-Control (or ETag) headers to GET /api/media/{id} — current implementation re-downloads from object storage on every public homepage load.
Store cover_image as a relative /api/media/{id} path, not an absolute URL, so images survive an origin change.
Optional: image thumbnail preview in ProjectManager after upload.
critical_code_review_comments: schemas.SiteSettingsUpdateRequest uses `settings: dict` with no shape validation — the endpoint is admin-only but still risky; a broken payload cascades to public routes.

public.get_site_content and public.calculate_project both do `settings['services']` / `settings['calculator']` without a None guard — if site_settings document is ever missing they'll 500 instead of falling back.

services/storage.py stores a global storage_key without a lock, and re-raises requests exceptions upward — an object-storage 5xx will surface to the admin as a bare 500. Wrap in HTTPException(502) with a friendlier message.

dashboard.upload_project_media does `file.filename.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]` without validating that the extension matches the content_type (e.g. content_type=image/png but filename=evil.svg). Low risk (storage proxy re-serves with the DB-recorded content_type) but tighten anyway.
PricingEditor rebuilds pricing from labels map on every save — silently loses any pricing row whose calculator key was removed and any custom copy in `note`.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of admin editor + public integration flows verified (admin login, editor rendering, pricing save+restore, portfolio upload+publish, public site reflects change, mobile layout no overflow, founders/contact intact)

seed_data_creation: During iteration 2: several TEST_ prefixed portfolio projects (e.g. 'TEST Media Project <hex>', 'TEST UI Project <hex>') and their uploaded 1x1 PNG media docs in db.media_files. All safe to remove by matching title LIKE 'TEST%' / created_at > now-1h. Pricing/hero regressions were restored to original values after each test via admin PUT.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/ with backend_test.py (iteration 1 baseline) + test_admin_editors.py (iteration 2 new admin controls). Run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v. External preview URL from frontend/.env is source of truth for both backend and UI tests. The admin PUT /api/admin/site-settings overwrites the entire `public` settings doc — always fetch current settings, deep-copy, mutate, then PUT back (and restore original after regression). The PricingEditor UI regenerates the pricing list from the calculator base_prices on every save, so any custom pricing note beyond the calculator-keyed services is lost — flag if seen. /api/media/{id} is a proxy back to Emergent object storage; a 200 with image/* content-type and non-empty body is the success signal. Mobile drawer transparency (iter 1) and React duplicate-key warnings for feed/projects (iter 1 + iter 2) remain outstanding UI items for the main agent.
rca of the issue: No new critical bugs found in iteration 2 — the new endpoints (site-settings, media upload, /api/media/{id}, project create with cover_image) all pass integration tests and UI regression. The React duplicate-key warning first flagged in iteration 1 now recurs on the projects mapping too because portfolio projects legitimately share titles (multiple 'TEST Portfolio' entries from prior runs); root cause is `key={project.title}` in HomePage.jsx work-section. Fix: use project.id (or _id serialized) or fall back to slug/index. The PricingEditor save-list construction is a latent data-loss risk (rebuilds pricing from calculator keys, discarding any DB pricing entries outside those 5 keys) but did not surface in this test since the seeded pricing only contained calculator-keyed services.
